row.proto: void Ui_Style_Apply_StatePropertiesToElements(void *style_mgr, void *target, void *elem_list, int32_t state_hash, uint32_t arg5)
row.notes: For each 8-byte element in elem_list [+8,+0x10): gathers matching rule sets via callback FUN_144382860, dedups their states (0x20 entries at rule+0x28..+0x30) by name (hash/len/strcmp), builds per-state lists (0x30 entries) of properties (0x40 entries keyed by id at +4), resolves missing value objects from the table at style_mgr+0x30..+0x38, applies per-component overrides (ids 0x2b5e6..0x2b5ff) to vec3 (type 0x14612be88) and vec4 (0x14612b9d8) values. Then picks the state whose name hash == state_hash (0x1505 matches unnamed), looks up each property descriptor in style_mgr+0x10..+0x18, widens the value to a vec4 (vec4/vec3/float/bool) and calls target vtable +0xd0(target, elem, desc, &vec4, arg5) when (desc+8 & ~2)==0. Callers 0x1442fc140 and 0x1442fdac0: after FUN_1442fcb00(elem, name, 0) apply state hash 0x597902 with arg5=0x1505 to elem+0x168; Ui_TextElement_Slot47 applies state *(*(elem+0x1b8))+0x68. style_mgr comes from global 0x146ca6de0 vtable +0x50. Good hook to observe style property pushes. (lab L1 re-check with caller context 2026-11-27)
